title: Pitti Engineering Ltd-$ - 513519 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Pitti Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹529 crores, with adjusted EBITDA margin at 16.8% and Lamination FY27 volume target raised to 82,000 tons.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 16% YoY to ₹529 crores and adjusted EBITDA rose 14% to ₹89 crores, with margin at 16.8%. Adjusted PAT was ₹32 crores versus ₹26 crores a year earlier. Lamination and assembly volume grew 19% to about 19,200 tons, and management raised its FY27 Lamination target to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons. Management said the ₹150 crore capex (sheet metal capacity now 108,000 tons) has just commenced, while the ₹290 crore Hyderabad greenfield casting project is about ₹60 crores spent. Margins were flat YoY, which management attributed to pre-operating manpower and variable costs ahead of operating leverage.

financial_highlights.change: Flat-ish vs prior year per Q&A

financial_highlights.value: ~₹491 crores as of Q4 FY26 end

financial_highlights.metric: Finance cost interest and bank charges

financial_highlights.change: Q1 lower due to deferred tax on right-of-use assets

segments.name: Traction Motor and Railway Components
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 28% of Q1 revenue; management flagged some softness in traction motors this quarter.

segments.name: Power Generation
segments.commentary: 15% of revenue. Data Centers (power generation side) at 5% of revenue, with direct US exports for one customer and domestic supply plus re-export for others.

segments.name: Industrial and Commercial / Mining, Oil & Gas / Special Application Motors
segments.commentary: Industrial and commercial 12%, Mining, Oil & Gas 10% (up from ~5% of revenue per management), Special Application Motors 9%. Renewable energy 3%, other 17%.

segments.name: Machine Components vs Casting
segments.commentary: Machined components growing faster than raw castings; machining utilisation 86% (vs 82%) is the main bottleneck, not order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Lamination volume target raised to 82,000 tons from 78,000 tons.
FY27 EBITDA guided at roughly ₹370 crores based on current outlook.
Management expects overall margins to improve as sheet metal utilisation moves toward 80%; did not quantify quarterly path.
Next year (FY28) at 90,000 tons operating level: turnover above ₹2,500 crores and EBITDA margin of about 17%-17.2% (ex incremental Lamination capex).
Casting capacity at 24,000 tons; casting volume guidance upgraded to about 17,000 tons (from ~16,000 previously referenced).
Export direct volumes expected to improve QoQ in Q2-Q4 as new capacity ramps.
Longer-term margin aspiration upwards of 18%, closer to 18%-18.5% in about three years, per management.
Effective tax rate for full FY27 expected around 25%.

Other income (state capex incentive) not expected this year; management leaning toward claiming from next year, dependent on government approval of 9-year period; ~₹70 crores of incentive receivable expected in 9-12 months.
capex_capacity: ₹150 crore capex recently commenced: sheet metal capacity raised to 108,000 tons, with casting and machining augmented.
₹290 crore greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad: ~₹60 crores spent so far (land acquisition started); ~30% infrastructure and ~70% plant and equipment; commissioning targeted by Q1 FY30.
Machining capacity to reach 1,080,000 machine hours from the ₹290 crore capex, added progressively each quarter; casting capacity now 24,000 tons.
Sheet metal headroom only ~8,000 tons at 80% operating efficiency; FY28 capacity capex expected around Q3-Q4 FY27 timeframe.
Potential Bangalore fully owned facility in FY28-FY29 (not board-approved): ~₹200 crores building plus ~₹200 crores equipment.
Sheet metal utilisation 73% (vs 70%), machining 86% (vs 82%), casting and fabrication 72%.
demand_pricing: China Plus One, Europe-to-India manufacturing shift and electrification cited as demand drivers; indirect exports via Indian operations of global customers growing.
Data Centers, railways, metros, mining and off-highway named as strong visibility areas; management cautious on AI data-center durability.
Mining order inquiries from US and Europe described as very good; Mining grew from ~5% to ~10% of revenue.

Growth in high value-added Lamination assemblies (rotor shaft, stator) driven by Data Centers, special industrial, mining, off-highway and wind; volume up ~37% per analyst calculation vs 16% for Lamination.
Direct exports flat (₹137 crores last year vs ₹139 crores this year per analyst), while domestic sales grew 23%.
Incremental LPG costs being passed through to customers per management.

qa_highlights.question: Which applications drive high value Stator and Rotor assembly growth (~37% volume vs 16% for Lamination), and what is EBITDA per ton for integrated assemblies?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is driven by Data Centers, special industrial, Mining, Off-Highway and wind. Management said integrated-assembly EBITDA per ton is hard to state because it depends on the Casting and Machining content, so it would not give a per-ton figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the export flatness a timing issue or customer delays, and are there new Data Center export customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports were roughly flat at about ₹137 crores last year vs ₹139 crores this year. Management expects QoQ improvement in Q2 to Q4 as new capacity ramps, and sees the bigger opportunity in indirect exports via Indian operations of global customers. The Data Center segment (5% of revenue) is mainly power generation, with direct US exports for one customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins flat despite better product mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Manpower and variable costs rose ahead of the ₹150 crore capex coming on stream. Management expects operating leverage to lift margins as utilisation rises toward 80%, and said Traction Motor softness is not the main margin driver.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ₹290 crore Hyderabad casting capex roadmap and Bangalore plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹60 crores spent, with land acquisition started; ~30% infrastructure and ~70% plant and equipment. No year-wise capex plan was given; commissioning targeted by Q1 FY30. Bangalore facility (not board-approved) would be ~₹200 crores building plus ~₹200 crores equipment, in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY28-FY29 volume and capacity plans, and when is the next capacity capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Sheet metal headroom is only ~8,000 tons at 80% efficiency on 108,000 tons capacity. FY28 capacity capex is expected around Q3-Q4 FY27. Management sees ~17-18% volume growth over three years but cautioned that Mining, Oil & Gas and Data Center demand can shift quickly.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt and why has interest cost not fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt was about ₹491 crores at Q4 FY26 end, with a further ~₹20-30 crores of working capital release possible (later stated as ₹20-25 crores). Interest and bank charges were ~₹19.6 crores plus ~₹3 crores forex loss, versus ~₹1 crore forex in Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will the state capex incentive (other income) run in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The earlier ₹220 crore capex incentive is exhausted. The ₹400 crore expansion would yield ~₹40 crores a year, but the eligibility certificate covers a 7-year period. Management expects no incentive income this year, and about ₹70 crores receivable in 9-12 months; a 9-year period, if approved, could change timing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and PAT targets apply for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA is roughly ₹370 crores on current outlook. FY28 at 90,000 tons: turnover about ₹2,500 crores and EBITDA margin 17-17.2%, excluding incremental Lamination capex. No PAT target was given.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on operating leverage from the ₹150 crore capex; utilisation must move toward 80% from 73% sheet metal.
Machining utilisation at 86% is the bottleneck for Machine Components; the ₹290 crore Hyderabad casting project is only ~₹60 crores spent, with commissioning by Q1 FY30.
Data Center and Mining demand described as fast-growing but cyclical; management cautious on AI data-center durability.
Direct export volumes flat YoY; management expects QoQ improvement in Q2-Q4 FY27, which should be checked next quarter.
Other income from state incentive is not expected in FY27 and depends on government approval of a 9-year period; ~₹70 crores receivable in 9-12 months.
Finance cost stayed high due to forex (~₹3 crores in Q1 FY27); net debt at ~₹491 crores and working capital release capped at ~₹20-30 crores.
key_quotes: Our objective is to build capacity ahead of the demand curve.

We are seeing strong demand from customers such as Cummins, Marathon, Nidec, and are also developing opportunities with a couple of more marquee customers, at the same time, we remain mindful that the pace of AI Data Center investments may not be sustainable indefinitely.
That is the biggest bottleneck for us in terms of ability to grow the Machine Components. It is not the order book, the ability to build machines fast enough.
No, it will be about 25%, not 33%. This effective tax rate is about 25%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and volume targets, with the Lamination target raised to 82,000 tons. Cautious and evasive on margin timing, declining to quantify the quarterly margin path, and measured on Data Center and Bangalore capex, which is not board-approved.

adds.what: ₹150 crore capex sheet metal capacity raised to 108,000 tons (casting and machining augmented)
₹290 crore greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad (~₹60 crore spent); commissioning targeted by Q1 FY30
Potential Bangalore fully owned facility (~₹400 crore total), not board-approved, FY28-FY29

growth.why: Management raised FY27 Lamination volume target to 82,000 t (from 78,000 t) and guided FY27 EBITDA of roughly ₹370 crore and FY28 turnover above ₹2,500 crore at 90,000 t, backed by the ₹150 crore sheet-metal expansion just commenced and 73% sheet-metal utilisation, though the Hyderabad casting plant only reaches commissioning by Q1 FY30 and no FY27 revenue growth percentage was given.
